messages.content: My Python script keeps throwing a KeyError. Here's the code: data['user']['name']

The KeyError means the key you're trying to access doesn't exist in the dictionary. You can safely handle this with: `name = data.get('user', {}).get('name', 'default')`. The `.get()` method returns `None` (or your default) instead of raising an error.
